note: ONEWAY1u (D194 point 6): what `daoris remote` and `daoris browser` said for each case of their tests, run once through the CLI's TypeScript verbs before they retire, on a home of their own (`<home>`; the map at `<home>/remotes.json`, the browser's files where the home puts them). Each row: the words, the operation the command makes of them (`op` and `args`; a row of the `command` door is the verb's own grammar, held for the command tree's table), the files before (`remotes`, `favorites`, `settings`; null: none), the environment, the exit, the lines on each stream and the files after. A file that does not parse says the parser's own words, `<parse error>`. `DriverFilesTextTests` reads it row for row; a sentence the port changes on purpose says why under `changed`.

rows.name: remote add, an address with no scheme is refused before it is wired
err: daoris: `team.example.com:5177` is not an address a deployment answers at — one starts http:// or https://, e.g. `--url https://team.example.com`.

rows.name: remote add, without a url
err: daoris: `remote add aurora` needs the deployment's address — `--url https://…`. The workspace name keys the map; the url and the key are what speak to its server.

rows.name: remote add, without a workspace name
err: daoris: `remote add` needs a workspace name — e.g. `daoris remote add aurora`. The name is the workspace, and it is what a shared deployment declares itself to be.

rows.name: remote add, no Daoris home to write into

rows.name: remote remove, the workspace off the map
out: daoris: `aurora` is no longer wired on this machine.
Nothing at the deployment changed: the key stays valid there until an operator revokes
it, and what that workspace already fed stays where it is. This workspace now syncs
nowhere from here, silently — which is what having no remote has always meant.
